Wikipedia full-text search (“Vanuatu transgender prisoner”), the LGBTQ rights in Vanuatu article, and the World Prison Brief Vanuatu country page contain no information on transgender-prisoner placement (birth sex vs identity), special units, solitary/segregation practice, or documented cases/rulings.

records.name: Nauru

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Nauru (Wikipedia) — Nauru Regional Processing Centre Rules 2014 gender-identity non-discrimination clause
adds.summary: Wikipedia's LGBTQ rights in Nauru article documents the only detention-related gender-identity provision found for Nauru: the Nauru Regional Processing Centre (RPC) Rules 2014, made under the Asylum Seekers (Regional Processing Centre) Act 2012, ban discrimination against any person based on sex or gender, sexual preference or gender identity within the RPC immigration-detention facility. This covers immigration detention, not Nauru's criminal-justice prison system, and concerns non-discrimination rather than placement by birth sex vs identity, special units, or solitary-confinement practice. No documented data was found on where transgender prisoners are housed in Nauru's corrections system, nor any trans-prisoner case or ruling.

records.note: Nauru: no criminal-prison trans-housing data found. The sole detention-relevant datum is the RPC Rules 2014 gender-identity non-discrimination clause, which applies to the immigration-detention centre rather than the prison system. Wikipedia full-text search, the LGBTQ rights in Nauru article, and the World Prison Brief Nauru page yielded nothing on trans-prisoner placement, special units, or solitary/segregation practice.
